newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures edge lower in narrow trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures edge lower in narrow trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended slightly lower Monday in thin, narrow trading in tandem with weaker natural gas futures.
"A lot of people are looking for direction, and they are looking at gas for direction for the summer months," said one Dallas-based futures trader.
Natural gas demand for power generation, especially in the Southwest, increases during the summer cooling season.

June California-Oregon Border futures settled down one cent at $13.30 a megawatt hour (MWh) after traded in a five cent range. July COB ended down seven cents at $15.63. Other COB months finished unchanged to 10 cents lower.

June Palo Verde (PV) futures settled down eight cents at $18.28 after bouncing between $18.00 and $18.35. July and August PV ended unchanged at $22.80 and $25.00, respectively. Deferred PV contracts finished eight to 10 cents lower.
June Henry Hub natgas futures settled down 45 cents at $2.081 per million British thermal units.
Cash power values in the western market were generally softer than Friday's as hydroelectric output in the Northwest continued to increase, market sources said.
Day-ahead firm, peak power prices at COB were quoted at $15.75-16.50 and at PV $16.50-17.00.
Market sources said June futures would likely take cue in the short-term from the cash and natgas prices.
"The dailies (next-day prices) are waiting to see how well people cover for May," said a Houston futures trader.
In the Pacific Northwest, forecasters called for temperatures to average near or slightly below normal through the week with above normal precipitation.
In the Southwest, dry and very warm weather would settle over the southern part of the region with readings averaging six to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal.
Cloudy skies and seasonable temperatures were predicted for Utah, Colorado and northern California.
NYMEX estimated 385 COB and 271 PV contracts were sold, down from Friday's 635 COB and 808 PV lots.
